newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses stage recovery as Dow rallies.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses stage recovery as Dow rallies.

text.p: A bullish start on Wall Street on Tuesday reversed early losses on European stock exchanges that were digesting Monday's spate of record highs.
London, Europe's biggest exchange, moved into positive territory on the back of Wall Street, which was up 24 points by mid-afternoon in Europe.
The London market suffered a sharp early dive when the government said shareholders would no longer be able to claim tax credits on share buybacks or special dividend payouts.
The surprise statement initially wiped almost 30 points off the blue chip FTSE 100 index. By the middle of the afternoon it had recovered to be up 4.2 points.

Dealers said the initial reaction to the tax ruling had been overdone and was exaggerated by players trying to trigger a break downwards in a market some believed had gone too far, too fast in recent weeks.

They said that although the timing of the British Treasury's announcement had been a surprise, its content was not. They noted that companies would still continue to generate cash and find alternative ways to funnel funds to shareholders.
In Frankfurt, German shares ended floor trading weaker, before Wall Street opened, but post-bourse electronic trading reversed most of the losses.
Sportswear maker adidas rose sharply after it announced it would be an official sponsor for the 1998 soccer world cup.
The Paris bourse also turned positive in the afternoon and was up about half a percentage point by 1430 GMT.
Debt-mired Eurotunnel slipped in heavy business on its first day of trade after a massive restructuring deal was agreed with banks.

On the currency markets the dollar firmed slightly after an early slip against the mark. Dealers said the market was grasping for news and little or no movement was expected before Friday's U.S. producer prices and retail sales figures.

Dealers said worse-than-expected German unemployment figures announced on Tuesday had done little to erode confidence in the mark, which was trading at around 1.5268 to the dollar at 1430 GMT. The dollar was likely to find strong support around the 1.52 mark area, they said.
There was a 39,000 rise in seasonally-adjusted pan-German unemployment against expectations of no change.
Against the yen, the dollar was steady at just above the 111.00 yen level, slightly above session lows.

Monday's comments from senior Japanese politicians about raising rates after this month's general election were taken lightly by the market but have created an air of caution over aggressive yen sales, dealers said.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5268 marks and 111.20 yen compared with 1.5299 marks and 111.22 yen late in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 4.2 points to 4,035.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 10.00 at 2,161.55.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 11.47 at 2,691.17. The electronic IBIS DAX was down 1.26 at 2703.95.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at 380.85 on Tuesday afternoon compared with $380.15 at the London close on Monday. Silver was unchanged at $4.90.
